items.title: HTTP status code groups
items.body:
1xx informational   2xx success   3xx redirection
4xx client error    5xx server error

items.title: Common 2xx and 3xx codes
items.body:
200 OK                 201 Created (new resource)
202 Accepted           204 No Content (success, empty body)
301 Moved Permanently  302 Found (temporary redirect)
304 Not Modified (cache is still valid)
307 / 308 redirect that keeps the HTTP method
items.description: Success and redirect codes you will see most.

items.title: Common 4xx codes
items.body:
400 Bad Request          401 Unauthorized (not authenticated)
403 Forbidden (no permission)   404 Not Found
405 Method Not Allowed   409 Conflict
410 Gone                 415 Unsupported Media Type
422 Unprocessable Content (validation failed)
429 Too Many Requests (rate limited)
items.description: Client error codes and when to use them.

items.title: Common 5xx codes
items.body:
500 Internal Server Error   501 Not Implemented
502 Bad Gateway (bad reply from upstream)
503 Service Unavailable    504 Gateway Timeout

items.title: HTTP methods: safe and idempotent
items.body:
GET      read            safe, idempotent
HEAD     headers only    safe, idempotent
POST     create/action   not idempotent
PUT      replace         idempotent
PATCH    partial update  usually not idempotent
DELETE   remove          idempotent
OPTIONS  capabilities / CORS preflight
items.description: Which methods can be repeated or cached safely.

items.title: Important request headers
items.body:
Content-Type: application/json     body format
Accept: application/json           desired response format
Authorization: Bearer <token>      credentials
User-Agent: my-app/1.0
If-None-Match: "<etag>"            conditional request

items.title: Important response headers
items.body:
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: max-age=3600       or: no-store
ETag: "abc123"
Location: /items/42               (after 201 or a redirect)
Retry-After: 30                   (with 429 / 503)
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer          (with 401)

items.title: CORS headers
items.body:
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400
items.description: What the server must return to allow a browser cross-origin call.

items.title: Auth: Bearer token
items.body: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer {{token}}" https://api.example.com/me
items.description: Send a token (JWT or OAuth access token) in the Authorization header.

items.title: Auth: Basic
items.body:
curl -u {{username}}:{{password}} https://api.example.com/me
# header form: Authorization: Basic base64(username:password)
items.description: Username and password; curl encodes them as base64 for you.

items.title: Auth: API key
items.body:
curl -H "X-API-Key: {{api_key}}" https://api.example.com/items
# avoid ?api_key=... in URLs: they end up in logs
items.description: Key in a custom header (or, less safely, a query string).

items.title: curl GET with query parameters
items.body:
curl -G https://api.example.com/items \
  --data-urlencode "q={{query}}" \
  -d "limit=10" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

items.title: curl POST JSON
items.body:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/items \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "{{name}}", "price": 9.99}'

items.title: curl PUT JSON
items.body:
curl -X PUT https://api.example.com/items/{{id}} \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "{{name}}", "price": 12.50}'

items.title: curl PATCH JSON
items.body:
curl -X PATCH https://api.example.com/items/{{id}} \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"price": 11.00}'

items.title: curl DELETE
items.body: curl -X DELETE https://api.example.com/items/{{id}} -i

items.title: curl form and file upload
items.body:
curl -d "user=ada&pass=secret" https://example.com/login
curl -F "file=@report.pdf" -F "title=Report" https://example.com/upload

items.title: curl: show status code and timing
items.body: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" https://example.com
items.description: Quiet request that prints only metrics.

items.title: curl: debug a request
items.body:
curl -v https://example.com            # verbose request/response
curl -L https://example.com            # follow redirects
curl -I https://example.com            # response headers only
curl --max-time 10 https://example.com
items.description: See headers, follow redirects, set a timeout.

items.title: curl: cookies
items.body:
curl -c cookies.txt -d "user=ada&pass=secret" https://example.com/login
curl -b cookies.txt https://example.com/account
items.description: Save and reuse cookies across requests.

items.title: REST URL design
items.body:
GET    /items            list (support ?page=&limit=&sort=)
POST   /items            create -> 201 + Location header
GET    /items/{id}       read
PUT    /items/{id}       replace
PATCH  /items/{id}       partial update
DELETE /items/{id}       delete -> 204
Use plural nouns, no verbs in paths, and version the API (/v1/items).
